title: Ordinary global Hom limit model of a resolved strict mapping tower
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l and X a scheme. Let I be a K-injective complex of strict towers of modules over the completed integral coefficient sheaf on X, and assume every term I^q is an injective tower. On the opposite category of all source complexes P, the strict constant-ring-sequence internal derived Hom from const(QP) to QI, followed by derived integral sections and the total derived limit of integral module towers, is naturally isomorphic to Q(lim_n Γ_R(Hom(P,I_n))). Γ_R and its scalar map are those of lem-coef-integral-dualizing-resolved-global-hom. The ordinary limit is taken in complexes, with all signed differentials and postcomposition transitions. This assertion concerns the mapping-tower side only, and involves no integral dualizing limit in module sheaves.

source.place: section-global-RHom (Tag 0B6E), section on internal Hom (Tags 0A95, 0A96), lemma-derived-limit-is-ok (Tag 0941); current blueprint prop-coef-integral-dualizing, second proof paragraph.

proof.text: Use the no-limit sequence-site comparison to identify the ambient derived mapping tower naturally in all source complexes with Q of the explicitly transposed strict global Hom cochain tower.

For an injective tower each successor transition splits. In degree q the Hom-complex product projections construct a section of postcomposition by a degreewise split epimorphism. Applying the specified additive module-valued sections preserves that splitting. Thus every transition of the strict global Hom tower is degreewise epic. This is proved by private helpers homComplex_post_split and resolvedMappingCochains_epi.

For a strict complex of module towers with degreewise epic transitions, solve 1-shift on its product degreewise. Identify the ordinary limit with the kernel. The degreewise-epic kernel-to-shifted-mapping-cone comparison identifies its actual inclusion roosι as a quasi-isomorphism, using the two cone coordinates. The natural normalized Roos comparison then proves invertibility of the canonical right-derived-limit unit at that complex. These are private helpers moduleRoosInclusionQuasiIso and moduleLimitUnitOfSurjective.

Whisker the canonical right-derived-limit unit by the strict cochain functor. Its components are invertible by the previous step, so it is a natural isomorphism. The source library functorEquivalence.inverse constructs the transpose; transposing back is definitionally the original tower of complexes. The natural strictTowerLimitIso identifies limit of complexes with termwise limit. Compose these isomorphisms with the no-limit comparison.

theorem integralDualizing_resolved_mappingLimit
    (I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E X) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] (hinj : ∀ q : ℤ, Injective (I.X q)) :
    Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.op ⋙
      integralDualizingAmbientMappingTower l E X (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I) ⋙
        CoefTower.totalLimit (integralDualizingCoefficients l E) ≅
      integralDualizingResolvedHomLimit l E X I)
